The two queens already placed occupy rows 1–2, columns 2 and 5, and regions A and B. The only remaining cells of region C therefore lie in column 1 (rows 3 and 4). The only remaining cells of region D therefore lie in columns 2–3 (but column 2 is already occupied). Consequently the unique pair of non-attacking placements that also leave a legal cell for E is D at (3,3) together with C at (4,1). (Any other choice for those two regions produces an immediate adjacency or a missing region.)
